name: pocketty

hlido_opinion.headline: A tightly-built iPhone/iPad SSH companion for answering blocked coding agents from your pocket — serious about end-to-end security and upfront about a one-time price, but bound to the 'herdr' orchestrator.
hlido_opinion.body: pocketty answers a real, specific pain: a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, opencode) blocks or finishes while you are away from the keyboard. It pushes an end-to-end-sealed alert only your phone can open, then drops you into that exact pane over SSH — Face ID, keys in the Secure Enclave, routed over Tailscale with no server in between — where you can send real keystrokes, review the turn's diff, dictate or paste a full message, preview a dev-server port, and see every agent's live state. The eight-step walkthrough is clear and the security architecture is described concretely (HPKE, X25519, ChaCha20; the relay stores nothing), which is more rigour than most companion apps offer. Pricing is refreshingly plain: 14 days free, then a one-time $99 (launch price, usually $129). The limiting factor is coupling — pocketty is explicitly 'made for herdr,' so its value depends on running that orchestrator — and it is iOS-only. For herdr users this looks excellent; for everyone else it is not yet a standalone pick. We did not exercise the app.

tier_rationale: STEADY (74): a focused, well-engineered product with a credible, concretely-described security model and honest one-time pricing. Held below higher bands by tight coupling to the 'herdr' orchestrator, an iOS-only footprint, and an unexercised app on a public-surface pass.
what_it_does_well: Solves a concrete problem — answer a blocked/finished agent from your phone, in a real terminal over SSH
Concrete, serious security model (end-to-end sealed alerts, Secure Enclave keys, Tailscale, relay stores nothing)
Rich interaction set: real keystrokes, per-turn diffs, dictation/paste, dev-server port preview, live multi-agent view
Honest, upfront pricing — 14-day trial then a one-time $99 (launch), not a subscription
what_it_fails_at: Tightly coupled to the 'herdr' orchestrator — value depends on running herdr, not standalone
iOS/iPadOS only; no Android or web path
App behaviour and the security claims could not be exercised on a public-surface pass
best_for: Developers already running 'herdr' who want to supervise coding agents away from the desk
People who want a security-serious, no-subscription mobile way to unblock agents
not_recommended_for: Developers not using herdr, for whom it is not yet a standalone tool
Android users or anyone needing a web/desktop client

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: An agent-ops companion: it surfaces and lets you answer coding agents (Claude Code/Codex/opencode) managed by herdr over SSH, rather than exposing a programmatic surface other agents call.

claims.claim: Only your phone can read the alert.
claims.evidence: End-to-end sealing described concretely (HPKE, X25519, ChaCha20; computer seals the alert for this phone only; the relay forwards/stores nothing).

claims.claim: Answer a blocked or finished agent in a real terminal over SSH, with real keystrokes and the turn's diff.
claims.evidence: Walkthrough shows opening the exact pane over SSH (Face ID, Secure Enclave, Tailscale), sending Return/Esc/Ctrl/arrows, and swiping for the turn's diff.
